25 Which statement about electromagnetic waves is correct?
m is invisible to the human eye.
A
A wave of wavelength 5.0  10–6
B
They can all travel at different speeds in free space.
C
They cannot be polarised.
D
They consist of vibrating atoms.

hints: Convert the given wavelength $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ to nanometres and compare it with the visible range of about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$.
Recall the two universal properties of all electromagnetic waves in free space: speed $c$ and transverse nature allowing polarisation.
Check whether $5000 \text{ nm}$ lies in visible light or in infrared, and whether the other statements confuse electromagnetic waves with mechanical waves.
walkthrough: Identify the test value: wavelength $\lambda = 5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$. Convert to nanometres: $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 5000 \text{ nm}$.
State the visible spectrum limits: human eye responds to about $400 \text{ nm}$ violet to $700 \text{ nm}$ red.
Compare: $5000 \text{ nm} > 700 \text{ nm}$, so this wave is infrared and invisible to the human eye.
Check the other statements: all electromagnetic waves have speed $c$ in free space, all can be polarised because they are transverse, and they are oscillating $E$ and $B$ fields that need no atoms.
Therefore only the statement about the $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ wave being invisible is correct. This is option A.

A.explanation: Wavelength $5.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 5000 \text{ nm}$ is in the infrared region, outside the visible $400-700 \text{ nm}$ range, so it is invisible.

B.explanation: In free space all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are transverse and so they can be polarised.

D.explanation: They consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, not vibrating atoms, and need no medium.
